reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the formation of an HfZr transition layer via Zr diffusion and its chemical bonding role, but provides no data on oxidation resistance, barrier function, or stability at 1600 °C, leaving most mechanistic and performance premises unsupported.
premises: Zirconium diffuses from VZrHfNbTa into a hafnium coating during high-temperature sintering
This diffusion forms an HfZr alloy transition layer at the interface
The HfZr layer chemically bonds the coating to the substrate
The HfZr layer acts as a diffusion barrier and promotes protective HfO2 formation
This mechanism suppresses internal oxidation and improves structural stability at ~1600 °C
